context: Do not fix 65 bundles one at a time. Group the failures by error text first -- the write_primitives DataFusion and SQLite clusters alone are five of the worst bundles -- and establish for each cluster whether it is an unimplemented operation (in which case the honest answer may be to withdraw those cells rather than fix them), a query-translation defect, or a real engine limit worth recording. Only then decide per cluster: fix, withdraw, or document as a known limitation. The corpus validator's >=3-platform rule means withdrawing a platform from a cohort may drop the whole cohort, so check that before withdrawing anything.
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-24 by building the Explorer snapshot from develop's corpus and querying it directly, not estimated.

  ranking-eligible                 82 of 211
  excluded: failed_queries         65
  excluded: no_queries             60
  excluded: insufficient_query_coverage   3
  excluded: insufficient_valid_queries    1
  trust labels                     211/211 maintainer-run, zero trust_not_rankable

The 60 no_queries bundles belong to dataframe-results-can-never-be-submitted-no-compliance-class (all DataFrame, root-caused, fixed forward in PR #1866). THIS item is the other 65: bundles that executed queries and had some fail. They are all validation=partial.

The exclusions are correct and specific -- the leaderboard is honest, and nothing here misleads a reader. The problem is depth: the public corpus advertises 211 results and ranks 82.

Worst offenders by failure count:
  write_primitives DataFusion SQL   324/351 failed, three bundles across SF0.01/0.1/1
  write_primitives SQLite SQL       252/351 failed, two bundles
  clickbench DataFusion DataFrame   129/129 failed, total
  read_primitives SQLite SQL        120/456 failed
  tpcdi DataFusion SQL               78/114 failed

By execution mode the split is even: 36 SQL, 29 DataFrame -- so unlike the no_queries class this is not a DataFrame-path defect. The concentration in write_primitives and read_primitives on DataFusion and SQLite suggests unimplemented operations rather than a single wiring bug, but that is a hypothesis and has not been verified.

Not filed as a launch blocker: the site is accurate today. Filed because 61 percent of the corpus not ranking is a product-quality question a reader will notice.

---

## LARGELY SUPERSEDED BY THE 2026-08-23 TRUST CUT — re-measure before acting (noted 2026-08-29)

The 2026-08-24 measurement above is against a corpus that no longer exists. PRs #1939 (develop) and #1940 (published-results) withdrew all 130 bundles run before 2026-08-23.

Re-measured against the post-cut snapshot built from the 9 surviving bundles:

  ranking-eligible          8 of 9
  excluded: failed_queries  1
  excluded: no_queries      0

Of the 65 failed-query bundles this item was opened for, exactly ONE survives: tpcds_sf10_spark_sql_20260823_233540_e9faf36f.json, with a single failed query. The write_primitives DataFusion and SQLite clusters named in the approach are gone with the bundles.

The item is not fully obsolete: the class of problem returns as soon as coverage is rebuilt, and the surviving Spark SF10 failure is a live instance worth root-causing on its own. But the cluster analysis in the work log describes data that is no longer checked in, so do not act on those groupings directly.

Suggest re-scoping to the one surviving failure plus a policy for new results, and re-measuring after restore-corpus-coverage-after-20260823-trust-cut adds cohorts back.

work_units.evidence: Grouped all 69 bundles in results-data/ carrying failed queries into 9 distinct error clusters: SQL dialect incompatibilities (23), Other/Uncategorized (15), DataFusion/UnifiedExpr translation (15), Transaction Primitives/DDL (5), Spark/DataVault column unresolved (3), TPCHavoc unsupported routines (2), PySpark window functions (2), Spark Flight Data type translation (2), Spark internal error (1), Query validation failure (1).
work_units.summary: Group the 65 bundles by failure error text and report the cluster sizes

work_units.evidence: Categorized root causes across clusters: (1) SQL dialect/unsupported functions: engine limit/dialect gap (e.g. DATE_TRUNC, COPY in SQLite); (2) UnifiedExpr/DataFusion: translation bugs/unimplemented operators; (3) DataVault/load_end_dts: schema column naming mistranslation; (4) Spark Flight Data: PySpark type argument error in adapter; (5) DDL/Write primitives: missing DDL features in embedded engines (SQLite/DataFusion).
work_units.summary: For each cluster, establish whether it is unimplemented, mistranslated, or a real engine limit
